frontage_ft_second_third_rate.source: english-georgian-townhouse proportional_system typical_ratios: 'Frontage 5.0-7.5 m for a second- or third-rate house, giving three bays'

frontage_ft_fourth_rate.source: english-georgian-townhouse proportional_system typical_ratios: '4.0-5.0 m and two bays for a fourth rate'

composition_parti.rule_append: The unit of composition is the terrace, not the house (governing_logic): two or three equal bays per house, the door taking one of them, repeated without variation along the run -- individual expression is confined to the doorcase, fanlight and door colour (hard constraint c05).

variants.note: The party-walled town-house case the family's own text names directly: 'the principal (usually first) floor is the tallest, because that is where the drawing room sits, one flight up from the street and noise.'

first_floor_ft.source: english-georgian-townhouse proportional_system typical_ratios: 'first floor 3.3-3.9 m (the tallest)'

height_proportion.rule_append: Applying the country-house ground-floor-tallest graduation to a terrace produces a facade that looks top-heavy and wrong (hard constraint c03) -- here the graduation peaks one storey up, at the drawing-room floor, and runs basement, ground, first (tallest), second, garret as a five-tier vertical social section rather than the free-standing house's four-tier decorative one.

ground_and_second_floor_ratio.source: english-georgian-townhouse proportional_system typical_ratios: '1.6:1 to 1.9:1 at ground and second floors'

first_floor_ratio.source: english-georgian-townhouse proportional_system typical_ratios: '2:1 to 2.4:1 at the first floor'

window_proportion.rule: Inverted from the country-house default: the tallest, most vertical sash sits one flight up at the drawing-room floor, not at the door (hard constraint c03). This replaces the wide, horizontal medieval mullion-and-transom window this slot would otherwise inherit through the corpus's deep Tudor-Jacobean ancestry, which has no place on a regulated Georgian terrace front at all.
sources: english-georgian-townhouse style node, proportional_system, constraint c03

variants.note: Gauged and rubbed brick reserved for openings and the entrance (english-georgian's own primary_cladding rule, inherited unchanged): a flat, thin, precisely jointed arch, not the deep, boldly keyed Baroque segmental head this slot would otherwise inherit from the sibling english-baroque node -- exactly the distinction the parent style names against its own Baroque ancestor ('a flat-arched or gauged-brick window head instead of a keyed segmental one').

window_head_masonry.rule: A flat gauged-brick arch, thin-jointed and precisely cut, replaces the Restoration/Queen Anne keyed segmental head -- one of the diagnostic differences the parent style states directly against its own Baroque ancestor.

door_surround.rule_append: This is the type's one licensed indulgence: 'a doorcase and fanlight that differ from house to house on a street where nothing else does' (diagnostic_tells). The Gibbs surround -- alternating rusticated blocks around the opening -- is an English device first given currency on Gibbs's own window architraves at St Martin-in-the-Fields, and it is what a London, Dublin or Edinburgh speculative builder actually worked from, not an American export reading of the same plates.

variants.note: 'Bound here, not at the trunk style, for a reason specific to this variant... the Gibbs surround is an ENGLISH device' (this node's own proportion_packs) -- replacing the Palladio-Ionic content this slot would otherwise inherit through the corpus's english-palladian branch, which is architecturally the wrong transmission line for a speculatively built terrace house whose builders owned Gibbs's own plates, not Leoni's or Ware's Palladio editions.
The plainer doorcase of the fourth-rate and lower third-rate house, where the budget does not run to a fanlight-and-pilasters frontispiece.

order.rule: The order appears at the doorcase only, and it is Gibbs's own -- the plates a London, Dublin or Edinburgh speculative builder actually owned -- not the Palladio-mediated reading the free-standing english-palladian style uses.

variants.note: The Palladian piano-nobile window-aedicule rule this slot would otherwise inherit does not apply -- this type has no rusticated basement and no piano nobile in the Palladian sense; ornament is confined to the doorcase alone (hard constraint c05), not distributed across a storey of window surrounds.
The Gibbs doorcase's own pilasters, the one place an applied order appears on the front at all (see door_surround, order).

pilaster.rule: The pilaster's only licensed appearance is flanking the doorcase; nothing else on the regulated street front carries one.

variants.note: 'Cornice or parapet line, floor levels, material and railing pattern must be continuous across the terrace. Individual expression is confined to the doorcase, fanlight and door colour' (hard constraint c05) -- replacing the Palladian licensed-points-only rule (centrepiece, piano-nobile aedicules, cornice) this slot would otherwise inherit, which assumes a free-standing composition this party-walled type does not have.

ornament_vocabulary.rule: Ornament is licensed to exactly one point on the regulated street front: the doorcase, its fanlight, and the door's paint colour. Everything else -- cornice line, floor levels, material, railing pattern -- must match the neighbours exactly.
sources: english-georgian-townhouse style node, constraint c05, diagnostic_tells

variants.note: 'A vertical social section -- basement service, ground-floor dining, first-floor principal drawing room, bedroom floor, garret -- expressed in graduated window heights' (defining_characteristics). Privacy and status run up the section, not back through the plan the way a free-standing house organises them.

public_private_gradient.rule: Public and private gradient is vertical, not horizontal: the servants move in the basement and by a back stair, the family receives one flight up in the drawing room, sleeps above that, and the garret houses the servants again at the top -- the whole hierarchy legible from the street in the graduated window heights.

variants.note: 'The whole service life pushed down into a basement lit by an area cut in front of the pavement and up a back stair' -- coal delivered through a round iron plate into vaults under the pavement, servants sleeping in the garret behind the parapet (description, long).

service_zone_strategy.rule: All service function is pushed into the basement -- kitchen lit by the front area, coal taken directly into vaults under the pavement through an iron plate -- and connects to the family floors above by a dedicated back stair, never through the principal rooms.

depth_ft_max.source: english-georgian-townhouse constraint c04 (hard, tested): 'Plan depth not to exceed 12.5 m without a light well or closet-wing set-back'

depth_and_pile.rule_append: Front and back rooms are lit only from the two short ends of the lot; beyond a 12.5 m plan depth the middle of the plan goes dark without a light well or a closet-wing set-back (hard constraint c04) -- a constraint the free-standing country house, lit on four sides, never has to solve.

variants.note: 'A front area with railings, steps up to a raised entrance, and coal vaults extending under the pavement' (defining_characteristics) -- the area is a sunken trench admitting light to the basement kitchen, bridged by the front steps (diagnostic_tells).

area_width_ft.source: english-georgian-townhouse proportional_system typical_ratios: 'area 1.2-2.0 m wide and one full storey deep'

front_steps_risers.source: english-georgian-townhouse proportional_system typical_ratios: 'front steps 3-6 risers above pavement level'

street_relationship.rule: The house meets the street across a sunken front area with railings, bridged by three to six steps up to the raised entrance; round cast-iron coal plates set into the pavement mark the vaults beneath, and party walls run up through the roof as a fire break with no window permitted on the party-wall elevation (hard constraint c04).
sources: english-georgian-townhouse style node, defining_characteristics, diagnostic_tells, proportional_system, constraint c04
